title: Quantum Heuristic Separation of Comb Inequalities for the Travelling Salesman Problem
abstract: Comb inequalities are essential cutting planes for the travelling salesman problem, yet their separation remains computationally challenging. We propose a quantum heuristic separation algorithm for this family of inequalities. The algorithm uses a procedure that prepares a uniform superposition of all combs with a fixed number of teeth using polynomially many gates and qubits. As part of this procedure, we present a circuit that coherently encodes the Hamming weight of a data register in one-hot form in an auxiliary register. The separation algorithm then searches for violated inequalities using the Grover-Mixer Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz. Its running time is polynomial under prescribed polynomial budgets for the number of QAOA rounds, parameter optimization steps and samples gathered, although we provide no evidence that such budgets suffice to find a violated comb with constant probability when one exists. We provide an explicit circuit construction for the mixer unitary, the full problem Hamiltonian and a resource analysis.
summary: This paper introduces a quantum heuristic approach to tackle the difficult separation problem for comb inequalities used in solving the Traveling Salesman Problem. It utilizes the Grover-Mixer QAOA ansatz to search for violated inequalities within a quantum superposition of all possible combs. While theoretically polynomial under certain budgets, the authors caution that the practical sufficiency of these budgets remains unproven.
main_problem: The core problem is developing a quantum heuristic algorithm to solve the computationally challenging separation problem for comb inequalities, which are crucial cutting planes for the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP).
main_result: The authors propose a quantum heuristic separation algorithm using the Grover-Mixer Quantum Alternating Operator Ansatz (GM-QAOA) to search for violated inequalities.
method: The method involves preparing a uniform superposition of all relevant combs using quantum gates and then applying the GM-QAOA framework to search the state space for violations.
model_or_system: The underlying model is the TSP, formulated as an Integer Linear Program (ILP) whose relaxation requires finding violated comb inequalities. The quantum computation utilizes qubits and quantum circuits to encode and search the comb structure.

paper_structure: The paper moves from establishing the classical difficulty of the separation problem (TSP/comb inequalities) to proposing a quantum heuristic solution utilizing the GM-QAOA framework, detailing the necessary quantum circuit constructions and resource analysis.
why_interesting: It directly applies advanced quantum algorithms (QAOA, superposition preparation) to a hard combinatorial optimization problem (TSP), bridging quantum computation with classical mathematical programming theory.

Figure 5 illustrates the implementation of the multi-controlled E gate for n = 3. This circuit is inspired by a similar one presented by Kaye and Mosca [43]. Initially, qubit 0 of the Count register is prepared in the state |1⟩, while all other qubits in this register are initialized to |0⟩. A cascade of conditional swap gates (Fredkin gates [29]) is then applied, with the data qubits serving as controls. These data qubits correspond to the Mask register in Fig. 3 and to the Tj registers in Fig. 4. For each data qubit in state |1⟩, the |1⟩state in the Count register is shifted by one position.
